course.title: Excel — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first and practice-oriented Excel course covering spreadsheet fundamentals, formulas, data cleaning, lookups, dynamic arrays, Tables, charts, PivotTables, Power Query, Data Models, financial analysis, dashboards, accessibility, audit, automation and professional governance. Follows the attached 27-module, 262-topic curriculum.
course.version_assumptions: Feature support is version/platform/license dependent. Core explanations target contemporary Microsoft Excel, while legacy techniques are retained for compatibility. Every advanced function/tool must be verified against the learner’s environment.
prerequisites: No programming experience required for the core course
learning_outcomes: Create organized workbooks and maintain data quality.
Build, debug and verify formulas and functions.
Create clear charts, PivotTable reports and dashboards.
Develop financial scenarios and auditable calculations.
Assess compatible automation and data-modeling tools.
Apply accessibility, security, quality assurance and governance practices.
learning_roadmap: Stage 2: Modules 6–12 — formula and function proficiency.
Stage 3: Modules 13–17 — data management and visualization.
Stage 4: Modules 18–21 — analytics and business intelligence; check feature availability.
Stage 5: Modules 22–23 and 27 — professional development, QA and governance.
Stage 6: Modules 24–26 — optional automation and developer specializations.
Stage 7: Complete Project 12 — integrated business operations and analytics capstone.
course.core_modules: Modules 1–23 and 27; Modules 24–26 are parallel optional specializations with independent compatibility requirements.
course.status_note: Draft generated from the attached Excel curriculum and current official documentation. Requires editorial review, version-specific verification, and practical execution in a supported Excel environment before publication.

included_from_pdf: All 24 practical exercises as separate exercise files with synthetic data and protected solution files
All 12 Section D projects including capstone
Section E specialist track topics and official ecosystem references
Section F staged learning path represented in course metadata
Section G quality requirements represented as lesson/project review checks
notes: The 24 extra practical exercises use synthetic CSV files; they are not prebuilt Excel workbooks.
Current CodeLeaf exercise grading checks authored text only; it does not open or execute .xlsx files. Actual workbook output and project rubrics require human review.
Excel formulas, VBA, Office Scripts, DAX and Power Query examples are instructional snippets, not sandbox-executable code.
XP remains platform-owned; course files contain no reward overrides.
